questions.question: Behind a single load balancer, req.ip always shows 10.0.0.5 (the balancer). What is the correct fix?
options: app.set("trust proxy", 1) so Express reads the client IP from X-Forwarded-For for one trusted hop
app.set("trust proxy", true) in every environment
Read req.headers["x-forwarded-for"] directly without any configuration
Move the app off the load balancer
questions.explanation: Trust exactly the hops you have. true trusts every forwarded entry, letting clients spoof their IP and bypass IP-based rate limits.

questions.question: What does server.close() do in a graceful shutdown handler?
options: Immediately destroys all sockets, including in-flight requests
Restarts the server on a new port
Stops accepting new connections and calls back once existing connections have ended
questions.explanation: In-flight requests finish first. Add a hard timeout below the platform's grace period, and close the database pool after the server.

questions.question: Why is CMD ["node", "src/server.js"] preferred over CMD npm start in a Dockerfile?
options: npm is not installed in official Node images
The JSON exec form makes Node PID 1 so it receives SIGTERM directly; the shell form wraps it in a shell that may not forward signals
The exec form makes the image smaller
npm start always runs in development mode
questions.explanation: With the shell form, docker stop's SIGTERM can be swallowed, so your shutdown handler never runs and the container is killed after the timeout.

questions.question: Why should an Express app validate its environment variables when it starts?
options: Express 5 requires a config schema to boot
It encrypts the variables in memory
A missing or malformed value crashes the deploy immediately instead of failing on a later request
questions.explanation: Failing fast at startup surfaces misconfiguration during the deploy, where a health check or rollout can catch it.
